headline: SELKIRK DRILLS 9.3% CU, 7.4 G/T AU AND 54.9 G/T AG AT MINTO NORTH — 15.1% CUEQ OVER 5.4M IN YUKON PHASE 2
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines (TSX-V: SCMI, OTCQX: SKRKF) released Phase 2 drill results from the Minto Project in the Yukon on September 28–29, highlighting 9.3% copper, 7.4 g/t gold, and 54.9 g/t silver — equivalent to 15.1% CuEq over 5.4 metres — among the best intervals from a program that has now completed 52,485 metres in 224 holes. The Minto Project is a past-producing copper mine in the Yukon's Minto Copper Belt; Phase 2 is aimed at expanding the known resource and testing new targets at Minto North, where drilling is intersecting grades well above the thresholds that sustained commercial production at the mine. For retail investors tracking TSX-V copper names, Selkirk's Phase 2 results at grades this far above typical open-pit copper thresholds make it one of the higher-grade near-term copper development stories in Canada.

headline: MIATA HITS 35.25M AT 3.41 G/T AU INCLUDING 5.55M OF 15.36 G/T AU AT SELA CREEK — HIGH-GRADE SURINAME GOLD SYSTEM EXPANDS
snippet: Miata Metals Corp. (TSX-V: MMET, OTCQX: MMETF) reported September 29 drill results from the Jons Trend at its Sela Creek Gold Project in Suriname, intersecting 35.25 metres at 3.41 g/t gold including a 5.55-metre high-grade core of 15.36 g/t gold. The results are part of the ongoing 25,000-metre diamond drilling program and represent continued expansion of the high-grade mineralised system. Suriname's Greenstone Belt hosts Newmont's Merian (750,000 oz/yr) and IAMGOLD's Saramacca, providing geological context for the district potential. For TSX-V gold investors, the combination of a thick mineralised interval and a high-grade core is the type of result that typically drives resource estimate upgrades — the program remains focused on defining a NI 43-101 compliant resource.

headline: CENTINELA COPPER ENTERS MANDATORY MEDIATION — LEGAL STRIKE WINDOW OPENS OCT 13 AS DUAL CHILE SUPPLY RISK BUILDS
snippet: Following a 98.73% strike vote, the two unions at Antofagasta Minerals' Centinela copper mine — Minera Esperanza and Distrito Centinela, representing 708 workers — formally entered mandatory five-day government mediation on September 29, with a legal strike window opening as early as October 13 if talks fail. Centinela produced 240,400 tonnes of copper in 2025 and is one of Chile's top-five copper operations. The development adds to the risk already posed by BHP's Escondida — the world's largest copper mine at 1.2 million tonnes per year — which has been suspended since September 23 following a fatal accident. Chile accounts for approximately 27% of global copper mine supply; simultaneous disruptions at both Escondida and Centinela would represent the most concentrated supply shock to copper markets since Escondida's 48-day strike in 2017.

headline: BIG CHINESE BANKS SHUTTER RETAIL LEVERAGED GOLD FUTURES — AU(T+D) CONTRACTS ENDED AT ICBC, BOC AND CCB
snippet: Major Chinese commercial banks including ICBC, Bank of China, China Construction Bank and Postal Savings Bank ended retail client access to Shanghai Gold Exchange-linked leveraged precious metals contracts — the Au(T+D) and Ag(T+D) deferred delivery products — after the SGE directed the move on September 27–28. The decision follows extreme volatility in gold prices that drove margin requirements to as high as 140%, effectively making the leveraged products more expensive than the underlying trade. The move closes off a significant source of paper gold demand that amplified price swings during the 2025–2026 bull market. For junior gold mining investors, removing Chinese retail paper leverage is a structural shift: it reduces speculative momentum amplification on the upside, but also removes a source of leveraged selling pressure during corrections — a net positive for physical market fundamentals over the medium term.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD ADVANCES 'MINOTAUR' DISCOVERY AT VALENTINE — 27.3M AT 2.11 G/T AU IN NEW NEWFOUNDLAND TARGET AREA
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp. (TSX: EQX) reported September 29 continued near-mine exploration success at the Valentine Gold Mine in Newfoundland, with the Minotaur target — a separate discovery area outside the current resource — returning 27.3 metres at 2.11 g/t gold, while the Frank Zone at the Musselwhite Mine Trend returned 99.4 metres at 0.98 g/t gold. Equinox has drilled 36,315 metres year-to-date at Valentine in 2026, with the near-surface program now complete and underground drilling continuing. Valentine is one of Canada's newest operating gold mines; the Minotaur result suggests the broader district remains open for resource additions that could extend mine life well beyond current models — a positive signal for any junior developers in the Valentine trend looking for offtake comparables.

headline: BRIXTON WRAPS 2026 THORN DRILL SEASON — BEST HOLE 17.6M AT 1.47 G/T AUEQ IN GLENFIDDICH ZONE, NORTHWEST BC
snippet: Brixton Metals Corp. (TSX-V: BBB, OTCQX: BBBXF) has completed its 2026 drill season at the Thorn Project in northwest British Columbia, with Camp Creek results highlighting 58 metres at 0.50 g/t AuEq and a best intersection of 17.6 metres at 1.47 g/t AuEq in the Glenfiddich Zone near-surface high-sulphidation system. The 2026 program totalled 6,592 metres in 25 holes targeting gold-silver-copper mineralisation across multiple zones at the large-scale porphyry and epithermal Thorn system in British Columbia's Golden Triangle. The next step is a geological synthesis and updated drill target prioritisation for 2027. For retail investors following BC gold explorers, Thorn is a multi-target system where each season's results feed into a progressively better understanding of the overall geometry — the 2026 season establishes the Camp Creek high-sulphidation zone as a near-surface priority for the next program.
